findings.title: Threat Actor Abuses Agentic AI Pentesting Framework to Target South Korean Financial Institutions
findings.summary_md: Zscaler ThreatLabz analyzed an exploitation campaign in which a threat actor abused ARTEX, an open source agentic penetration testing framework developed in China that uses LLMs to automate reconnaissance and exploitation, to target South Korean financial institutions. First observed in late September 2026, the campaign affected multiple South Korean financial firms and resulted in exfiltration of personally identifiable information belonging to approximately 67,000 individuals. ThreatLabz assesses with moderate confidence the campaign is the work of a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking threat actor.

findings.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup Issue Investigation
findings.summary_md: ConnectWise published a status-page advisory on October 16, 2026 investigating unauthorized access associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup environment. The adversary gained access to application identities within the environment, and ConnectWise disabled seven affected application identities and revoked certificates, suspending Cloud Backup service. Microsoft later attributed the activity to Storm-0940, which used ARTEX to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants.

findings.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
findings.summary_md: Microsoft Threat Intelligence attributed to Storm-0940 a large-scale supply-chain compromise of ConnectWise Cloud Backup that used the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework to automate attacks against hundreds of organizations globally. Storm-0940 used ARTEX to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants after compromising ConnectWise application identities, and Microsoft advised reviewing service-principal sign-ins. ARTEX is a multi-agent LLM system written in Go with a Next.js frontend that can use any AI model.

findings.title: Disclosing the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor
findings.summary_md: Elastic Security Labs disclosed the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor on October 13, 2023, as part of the REF5961 intrusion set targeting governments and organizations in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. The backdoor targets x86 systems and uses a legitimate binary as an injection vehicle. BLOODALCHEMY was later observed deployed by VAPOR PANDA at a Middle East interior ministry and a Latin America foreign ministry.

findings.title: Re-reading the ARTEX Attacks on Korea's Financial Sector: AI Agents, Disposable VPS Infrastructure, and Non-Customer-Facing Systems
findings.summary_md: An independent researcher published a Shodan and Censys point-in-time analysis of ARTEX exposure on October 4, 2026, following AI-agent attacks against South Korea's financial sector. The post documents exposed ARTEX infrastructure, disposable VPS and proxy egress, and incident indicators of compromise, and notes the Korea Financial Security Institute briefed about 160 financial-sector security practitioners on AI-agent attacks on September 17, 2026. It argues AI agents reduce the cost of reconnaissance while disposable infrastructure reduces the cost of rotating egress.
